reads.summary: Map of five client-portal surfaces for redesign: (1) Notifications — there is NO /notifications page anywhere in the app; the entire surface today is the top-nav bell popover (components/tahi/notification-bell.tsx) over GET/PATCH /api/notifications, which returns a hard-capped 20 most-recent rows plus a true unread count, with no pagination, no read/unread filter, no entity filter, no delete/archive. TP.4 (TASKS.md:134) asks for an "All / Past notifications" page; the CSS hooks for the missing "View all" footer already exist and are dead (app-shell.css:531-533). (2) Account/profile — there is no /account route; the client's account IS /settings with an "Account" group (Profile, Appearance, Notifications) plus an "Organization" group (Organization, People, Brand) and "Plan & billing", assembled by components/tahi/settings/settings-shell.tsx. A client can change: their own name/role/phone (contacts row), their Clerk avatar and first/last name, device-level theme/reduce-motion/sidebar preference, per-event notification channels; and, only if portalRole === 'admin', the org name/website/industry/logo/brand-colour, the people roster, brand assets, and plan-change requests. Email, password, and 2FA have NO surface at all (no Clerk UserProfile/UserButton is mounted anywhere). (3) Onboarding — app/(onboarding)/onboarding (client) and /welcome (teammate), a link-driven persona flow rendered by components/tahi/onboarding-content.tsx; the "details" step's Company name, Role and Timezone inputs are uncontrolled and thrown away, and the "60-second hello" is a fake video (a still image with a ticking caption timer). A second onboarding exists: the ClientFirstRun checklist on the portal home (client-home.tsx:323) over /api/portal/onboarding. (4) Offline — a single static app/offline/page.tsx with no retry button, not listed as a public route in middleware.ts, so it sits behind the Clerk wall that the service worker precaching it cannot pass while signed out. (5) Portal roles — contacts.portalRole ('admin' | 'member', NOT NULL default 'member') is the client-admin signal, set by /api/admin/permissions/contact-role (MCP set_contact_portal_role); three different admin checks disagree with each other (strict portalRole in /api/portal/people, portalRole-or-isPrimary in lib/portal-access.ts, and a never-reached isPrimary fallback in settings-shell).
facts: NO NOTIFICATIONS PAGE EXISTS. `find app -path "*notification*" -name "*.tsx"` returns nothing; app/(dashboard)/ has no `notifications` directory. /notifications resolves to a Next 404 (no app/not-found.tsx or app/(dashboard)/not-found.tsx exists either, so it is the framework default page).

TP.4 ask, verbatim: TASKS.md:134 — "- [ ] TP.4 - [Design first, then FE] **Notifications page (not urgent).** An All notifications and Past notifications page: the full history behind the bell, simple list with read state. Design in Claude Design first. Low priority."
TP.4 is Tier 1 (client facing) in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-overnight-run.md:18, listed alongside account, onboarding, mobile bottom nav and the offline page.

GET /api/notifications (app/api/notifications/route.ts:14) returns `{ items, unreadCount }`. `items` is `drizzle.select()` with NO column projection (route.ts:23-28), so every row field ships to the client: id, userId (Clerk id), userType, eventType, title, body, entityType, entityId, read, createdAt (db/schema.ts:1128-1144).

GET /api/notifications is hard-capped at PAGE_SIZE = 20 (route.ts:9, :28), ordered `desc(createdAt)`. There is NO page/cursor/offset/limit parameter, no read-state filter, no entityType filter, and no date range. A 'Past notifications' page cannot be built on this endpoint as written.
unreadCount is a separate COUNT over the whole table, deliberately not derived from the 20-row page (app/api/notifications/route.ts:30-40), so the badge is true even past 20.

PATCH /api/notifications (route.ts:53) accepts exactly three body shapes: `{ all: true }` (marks every row for the user read, route.ts:75-79), `{ id }` (route.ts:80-89), and `{ entityType, entityId }` (route.ts:90-102). Anything else 400s with 'Provide id, all: true, or entityType + entityId' (route.ts:68-70). Every branch is scoped by `eq(notifications.userId, userId)`.
There is NO endpoint to mark a notification UNREAD, to delete one, or to archive one. `read` is a one-way flag.

Auth on /api/notifications is `getRequestAuth(req)` + `if (!userId) 401` only (route.ts:15-18, :54-57). There is no org check and no audience branch: the same route serves the Tahi team and clients, keyed purely on Clerk user id.

SSE stream GET /api/notifications/stream (app/api/notifications/stream/route.ts:34) polls D1 for the user's 10 newest UNREAD rows (:112-122), filters to `createdAt > lastCheckedAt` (:127) and emits `data: {type:'notification', notification}` per row (:135). It also emits `{type:'connected', userId}` on open (:99), `: ping` comments every 25s (:31, :155), and `{type:'reconnect'}` before self-closing at 5 minutes (:32, :162).

Stream poll cadence: 5s base, backing off +2.5s per empty poll to a 15s cap, with +-1s jitter, floored at 1s (stream/route.ts:27-30, :52-59). Response headers are text/event-stream, no-cache no-transform, keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no (:171-177).

The bell is the ONLY consumer of both endpoints: components/tahi/notification-bell.tsx, mounted once in components/tahi/app-top-nav.tsx:95 as `<NotificationBell audience={isAdmin ? 'team' : 'client'} />`.

Bell states, all present: loading = three animate-pulse skeleton rows with a 36x36 icon block (notification-bell.tsx:286-301); empty = leaf-less bell glyph + 'You are all caught up.' + small 'New activity will show up here.' (:302-309); populated = up to 20 `.notif-row` buttons (:311-341).

Bell row anatomy (notification-bell.tsx:311-341): 36px icon square (`.notif-ic`) with an entity-mapped glyph, an unread dot overlay (`.notif-dot`, :319), bold title (`data-private`, :322), optional one-line ellipsised body at 0.8125rem (:323-337, also `data-private`), and a relative timestamp (:338).

Bell icon mapping by entityType (notification-bell.tsx:45-55): request/invoice/message/task/organisation|client get their nav glyph; EVERYTHING else falls through to the generic bell icon. There is no per-eventType icon and no tone/colour by severity.

Relative time formatter (notification-bell.tsx:32-43): 'Just now' <1m, `${m}m ago`, `${h}h ago`, then `${d}d ago` forever — a year-old row reads '412d ago'. No absolute date is shown anywhere in the bell.
Bell header (notification-bell.tsx:270-283): h4 'Notifications' plus a 'Mark all as read' button that only renders when unreadCount > 0, showing 'Marking...' while in flight.

Bell unread affordances: button gets class `has-unread` and renders `.tb-bell-dot` (notification-bell.tsx:251, :258); aria-label is `Notifications (N unread)` (:253). The dot pulses via `bell-pulse` (app-shell.css:397).

Clicking a row (notification-bell.tsx:236-243): marks it read optimistically, closes the popover, then `router.push(href)` where href = `notificationHref(entityType, entityId, audience)`. When the resolver returns null the click only marks read and navigates nowhere.
Bell popover geometry: width 23.75rem, maxHeight 32rem, align 'end', `mobileFullWidth` (notification-bell.tsx:265-268), via components/tahi/popover.tsx.

Bell live-update path: initial fetch, then an EventSource with self-managed reconnect (1s, 2s, 4s... capped 30s + jitter, notification-bell.tsx:112-126); a clean `onopen` resets backoff AND refetches (:138-143). If EventSource is undefined it degrades to a 60s poll (:94-99). SSE arrivals prepend and increment the local count (:159-167).

Cross-surface sync: `window.dispatchEvent(new Event(NOTIFICATIONS_CHANGED_EVENT))` (lib/notification-events.ts:19, value 'tahi:notifications-changed'). Only ONE surface fires it: app/(dashboard)/requests/[id]/request-detail.tsx:859, after PATCHing `{entityType:'request', entityId}` on mount (:840-863). The bell listens at notification-bell.tsx:192-196.

The event vocabulary lives in lib/notification-links.ts:15-50 — 30 NotificationEventType values: request_status_changed, request_created, new_message, request_assigned, task_assigned, task_status_changed, invoice_created, invoice_paid, invoice_overdue, proposal_sent, proposal_signed, contract_sent, contract_signed, call_scheduled, deal_stage_changed, lead_assigned, schedule_published, announcement_posted, retainer_churn_risk, retainer_upsell_opportunity, delivery_off_track, subscription_change_requested, lead_high_intent, lead_idle_qualifying, affiliate_reactivation, finance_anomaly, daily_summary, content_ideation, cron_failed.

NotificationEntityType (lib/notification-links.ts:52-70): request, task, message, invoice, organisation, contract, proposal, call, deal, lead, schedule, announcement, subscription, affiliate, finance_anomaly, system, content_week, cron.

CLIENT route map (lib/notification-links.ts:132-161) — the only entities a client bell can navigate to: request -> `/requests/{id}` or `/requests`; invoice -> `/invoices` (LIST, not detail, because the detail page still calls /api/admin/invoices, :128-130); subscription -> `/billing`; organisation -> `/settings`; message -> `/requests`; announcement -> `/overview`. task, contract, proposal, deal, lead, schedule, call, affiliate, finance_anomaly, content_week, cron, system ALL return null (:146-158).

TEAM route map (lib/notification-links.ts:83-117) deep-links request/task/invoice/organisation/contract/proposal/deal/lead/schedule to detail pages, and lands message->/requests, call->/calls, announcement->/announcements, subscription->/billing, affiliate->/leads, finance_anomaly->/financial-reports, content_week->/content-studio?tab=ideas, cron->/settings/crons, system->null.

Notification rows are written only through lib/notifications.ts. Recipients are a typed union (`clerkUserId`, `teamMemberId`, `contactId`, `participantId`, `ownerSettingValue`, lines 53-58); the module resolves domain ids to Clerk ids in two batched queries (:94-157) and SKIPS anyone with no clerkUserId (:130-134), reporting `{delivered, skipped}`.

Every bell insert is filtered by the recipient's in-app preference first (lib/notifications.ts:170, via filterRecipientsByInAppPref, lib/notification-preferences.ts:203-211). Insert failures are swallowed and logged (:188-191); createNotifications never throws.

Client-facing audience emitter: `notifyOrgContacts(db, orgId, payload, audience?)` (lib/notifications.ts:538-558), optionally narrowed to contacts who can see the request's brand via brandContacts (`contactsForBrand`, :500-527: a contact with NO brand links sees everything).

Only THREE call sites ever notify client contacts: app/api/admin/requests/[id]/messages/route.ts:292 (type 'new_message', entityType 'request', gated on `clientVisible`), lib/request-status-effects.ts:165 (type 'request_status_changed', entityType 'request', skipped when request.isInternal or the status is in CLIENT_SILENT_STATUSES), and lib/automation-executor.ts:170 (whatever the automation rule specifies).

Client invoice bell rows come from app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/send-email/route.ts:223-230: type 'invoice_created', entityType 'invoice', title 'Invoice ready to pay' or 'New invoice', body `Invoice {ref} for {amount} {currency} is due {date}.` Written ONLY on first send (`!alreadySent`) and ONLY to billingContacts.

Notification preferences: table notification_preferences (db/schema.ts:1156-1175), unique on (userId, userType, eventType, channel). Resolution order is exact row -> per-user wildcard row (eventType '*') -> hardcoded DEFAULT_ENABLED { in_app: true, email: true, slack: false } (lib/notification-preferences.ts:10-14, :55-59, :73-99). Failures fail OPEN (send).

PREF_EVENT_TYPES, the events the send paths actually resolve (lib/notification-preferences.ts:34-46): request_status_changed, request_created, request_assigned, new_message, invoice_created, invoice_paid, invoice_overdue, announcement_posted. That is the whole list.

Client notification-settings UI (components/tahi/settings/sections/notifications.tsx:59-65) offers five rows: 'Request updates' (request_status_changed), 'New message' (new_message), 'Delivery ready' (delivery_ready), 'Invoice due' (invoice_created), 'Weekly summary' (weekly_summary). Channels for clients are Email + In-app only; Slack is team-only (:67-74).

Each channel chip is a `role="switch"` pill (`.ntf-ch`, notifications.tsx:180-196) that toggles OPTIMISTICALLY and reverts with an error toast on failure (:120-131). Absent stored rows resolve to DEFAULTS (in_app true, email true) via `resolved()` (:100-103).

Quiet hours renders as a single Toggle (notifications.tsx:201-209) persisted as eventType 'quiet_hours' / channel '*', defaulting ON (:105). Copy: 'Hold non-urgent notifications between 7pm and 8am. Mentions and overdue invoices still come through.'

Notification-settings footnote already hedges (notifications.tsx:210-214): 'In-app preferences apply immediately; email and Slack preferences apply as each alert adopts them. Transactional emails such as receipts and contracts always send.'

PATCH /api/portal/notifications validates against PREF_EVENT_TYPES + EXTRA_CLIENT_EVENT_TYPES ['delivery_ready','weekly_summary'] + the quiet_hours/'*' special case, and PORTAL_CHANNELS ['in_app','email'] (app/api/portal/notifications/route.ts:12, :20, :26, :34-41). Body is `{ updates: [{eventType, channel, enabled}] }`; upsert per row via onConflictDoUpdate (:101-122). GET returns `{ preferences: [{eventType, channel, enabled}] }` (:58-72); an EMPTY array is the honest 'everything at default' state.
Both notification-preference routes 403 an impersonating admin on PATCH ('Read-only in client view', portal route :85-87) but allow GET.

Announcements banner: components/tahi/announcement-banner.tsx, mounted unconditionally in app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:213 ABOVE the top nav and below the impersonation strip. Self-gating: returns null when the list is empty (:96).

Announcement banner fields rendered (announcement-banner.tsx:100-124): emoji (own `emoji` or a per-type default from EMOJI_BY_TYPE, :40-45), bold title, one-line ellipsised body, an optional CTA anchor rendered only when BOTH ctaLabel and ctaUrl exist (:103, :111-115, target=_blank rel=noopener), and a dismiss X with aria-label `Dismiss announcement: {title}`.

Announcement tones: info | success | warning | maintenance, anything else coerced to info (announcement-banner.tsx:37, :101). Chrome is hardcoded forest hex in app-shell.css:560-586, an explicitly sanctioned CLAUDE.md exception.

Announcement dismissal is dual-write: localStorage key 'tahi-dismissed-announcements' for instant hide (announcement-banner.tsx:47-66) plus POST /api/portal/announcements/{id}/dismiss which writes announcementDismissals server-side (:93).

GET /api/portal/announcements (app/api/portal/announcements/route.ts:11) requires userId AND orgId (401 otherwise), filters to publishedAt set and not expired (:36-40), then by targetType: 'all' | 'plan_type' (matched against organisations.planType) | 'org' (orgId inside the targetIds JSON array, falling back to targetValue) (:43-63), then removes rows the user has dismissed (:66-74). It returns id, title, body, type, publishedAt, expiresAt, emoji, ctaLabel, ctaUrl.
Announcement banner has NO loading state and NO error state: it fetches in a useEffect, silently swallows failures (:81-83) and renders nothing until data lands.

The client 'account' surface is /settings — app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx:8 (metadata 'Settings - Tahi Dashboard'), which passes isAdmin into SettingsContent -> SettingsShell. Clients SKIP the requirePageFeature('settings') gate entirely (page.tsx:18: `if (isAdmin) await requirePageFeature('settings')`).

Client settings IA (components/tahi/settings/settings-shell.tsx:68-70, :102-105, :113): CLIENT_GROUPS = ['Account', 'Organization', 'Plan & billing']. Account = Profile (User icon), Appearance (SunMoon), Notifications (Bell). Organization = Organization (Building2), People (Users, clientAdminOnly), Brand (Palette). Plan & billing = Plan & billing (Wallet).

Settings deep-links via `?section=<id>` applied post-mount, and `selectSection` keeps the URL in sync with replaceState (settings-shell.tsx:210-229). Section switch scrolls #main-content back to top (:234-236). Mobile uses a native <select> optgroup picker instead of the rail (:274-305).

isClientAdmin in the settings shell (settings-shell.tsx:171-180) comes from GET /api/portal/profile: `if (typeof c.portalRole === 'string') return c.portalRole === 'admin'`, with an isPrimary fallback only when portalRole is not a string. contacts.portal_role is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member' (db/schema.ts:124), so the isPrimary fallback is unreachable in practice and the in-file TODO at :168-170 is stale.

WHAT A CLIENT CAN CHANGE ABOUT THEMSELVES (Profile section, components/tahi/settings/sections/profile.tsx): Full name, Role/title, Phone — persisted to their contacts row via PATCH /api/portal/profile (:148-154). Email is rendered DISABLED (:244) with the line 'Email is managed through your login provider.' (:271-273). Avatar goes to Clerk via `user.setProfileImage` (:185); the workspace avatar mirror is admin-only ('Only team members have a workspace avatar column today', :165-168). Name changes also best-effort sync Clerk first/last name (:120-129).

Profile section states: skeleton with a 78px circle + four field blocks while Clerk or the record loads (profile.tsx:50-72, gated at :209-211); Save button disabled while saving or when name is empty (:266); toasts 'Profile saved' / 'Could not save your profile' / 'Profile photo updated' / 'Could not upload that image' / 'Profile photo removed' (:156-157, :188-190, :201-203).

GET /api/portal/profile (app/api/portal/profile/route.ts:11) returns `{ contact: { id, name, email, role, isPrimary, portalRole, phone }, orgId }`, matched on (orgId, clerkUserId). If no contact row matches it returns `{ contact: null, orgId }` with a 200 (:37-43) — the UI then has no record to save against and the Save handler silently no-ops (profile.tsx:147 `else if (contact)`).

PATCH /api/portal/profile accepts ONLY name, role, phone (route.ts:61-65, :84-86). It 403s the Tahi org, 403s an impersonating admin ('Read-only in client view', :57-59), 404s 'Contact record not found', and 400s 'No fields to update'.

Appearance section (components/tahi/settings/sections/appearance.tsx) is device-level localStorage only, all three: `tahi-theme` -> `.dark` on <html> (:23, :73-82), `tahi-reduce-motion` -> `.reduce-motion` (:24, :84-93), `tahi-sidebar-start-collapsed` (:25, :95-103). Lede: 'How the studio looks and feels on this device. Saved to this browser only.' A MutationObserver keeps it in sync with the sidebar's theme toggle, and a storage listener mirrors other tabs (:47-66).

Organization section (components/tahi/settings/sections/org.tsx) lets a client-admin edit name, website, industry, brand colour (hex + native colour input) and upload/remove a logo through the real R2 flow presign -> PUT -> confirm -> PATCH logoUrl (:126-172). Members see every field `disabled` (:192). PATCH /api/portal/organisation requires portalRole === 'admin' strictly (app/api/portal/organisation/route.ts:11-22, :82-87), 403s impersonation (:77-79), and validates hex as /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/ (:115).

People section (components/tahi/settings/sections/people.tsx) shows the org roster from GET /api/portal/people: avatar initials, name, email, a 'Pending invite' chip when clerkUserId is null (route.ts:78), and a level chip Owner (isPrimary) / Admin (portalRole 'admin') / Member (people.tsx:54-58). Only two levels are offered on write — 'The design\'s Viewer level has no portalRole backing, so it is intentionally not offered' (people.tsx:13-14).

People writes: POST creates a Clerk organization invitation FIRST and only records the pending contact row on success (app/api/portal/people/route.ts:132-160); PATCH refuses to demote the last admin with 409 'Your workspace needs at least one admin' (:208-218); DELETE refuses self-removal (409, :275) and refuses the primary contact (409 'The primary contact cannot be removed. Ask the studio to reassign it first.', :278-283) and revokes the Clerk invitation or membership before deleting the row (:288-310). Every write is gated on `requireClientAdmin` = portalRole === 'admin' STRICTLY, with no isPrimary fallback (:34-45).

People section states: 3-row animate-pulse LoadingShell (people.tsx:60-88); error EmptyRow 'Could not load your teammates. Try again shortly.' (:207); empty EmptyRow 'No teammates yet. Invite someone to get started.' (:209); members get 'Only workspace admins can invite or manage teammates.' (:239-243) and no RowActions; a newly created row gets a 1.4s `.lrow-enter` highlight (:124-127).

Plan & billing section (components/tahi/settings/sections/plan.tsx) is request-to-change only: every plan switch or track change POSTs /api/portal/subscription/change-request and flashes a note like 'Change to {plan} requested - your studio contact will confirm before it takes effect.' (:105-147). 'Manage payment method' opens the Stripe portal via GET /api/portal/billing/session and falls back to 'Payment management is not available yet. Your studio contact can help.' (:149-165). Members see disabled buttons with title 'Only workspace admins can change the plan'. Empty state when there is no subscription: 'No active plan yet' / 'Your studio contact is setting up your retainer.' (:324-336).

portalRole is set by POST /api/admin/permissions/contact-role (app/api/admin/permissions/contact-role/route.ts:20), accepting only 'admin' | 'member' (:13, :30-32), gated by requireManagePermissions + requireFeature('settings.permissions') (:23-26), and audit-logged as 'permission.portal_role_changed' with before/after (:49-58). The MCP tool `set_contact_portal_role` is declared at workers/mcp-server/src/index.ts:679-682 and proxies to that route at :1981-1984.

All three org-creation paths now stamp the primary contact portalRole 'admin': app/api/portal/provision/route.ts:126, app/api/admin/clients/route.ts:201, app/api/portal/accept-invite/route.ts:188. The comment block at lib/portal-access.ts:9-16 claiming they do not is STALE.

accept-invite promotion rule (app/api/portal/accept-invite/route.ts:167-169): `shouldOwn = !orgHasAdmin && (existing.length === 0 || !!match?.isPrimary)`. Everyone else lands 'member'. An existing admin is never demoted (:175).

lib/portal-access.ts:30-36 `isPortalAdminContact` returns true for portalRole === 'admin' OR isPrimary. This is the gate used for money surfaces (invoices, subscription amounts) and for the onboarding 'invoice me' path (app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:116).

Nav gating for clients: components/tahi/nav-model.tsx:122-146 CLIENT_NAV = 'Your project' (Overview, Requests), 'Library' (Files, Services), 'Billing' (Invoices, requiresOrgAdmin). Messages is deliberately removed for V1 (:128). Schedules/Contracts/Proposals were removed 2026-09-05 because their pages bounce a client (:113-121). filterNav hides requiresOrgAdmin items only when clientPortalRole === 'member' — null/unknown fails OPEN (:158-168, :191).

Mobile bottom nav (components/tahi/mobile-bottom-nav.tsx:38): CLIENT_PRIMARY_HREFS = ['/overview','/requests','/files'] plus a 'More' sheet that lists every filtered nav group with a pinned Settings row (:216-228). There is no notifications entry on either surface.

The account menu is components/tahi/sidebar-user-card.tsx (pinned bottom of the rail): avatar + name + email, and a popover with Theme (light/dark state readout), Private mode + Client view (super-admin only, :150-162), Settings link, and Sign out (:164-171). Clients get Theme, Settings, Sign out only.

Onboarding entry: app/(onboarding)/onboarding/page.tsx (metadata title 'Welcome to Tahi', :10). Unauthenticated -> redirect to /sign-in?redirect_url=... (:24-27). An invite token from ?token= or the `tahi-invite-token` cookie the middleware stashed (:32-37) is resolved server-side and WINS over any ?p= param (:60-86). Invitee PII (company/name/email) is only disclosed when the signed-in user's VERIFIED email matches the invite (:72-80). If publicMetadata.onboardingComplete AND an orgId exist, it redirects to /overview (:94).

Onboarding persona resolution (lib/onboarding-entry.ts:112-123): the ?p= query param is honoured ONLY when NODE_ENV !== 'production'. In production, with no token, every visitor gets the 'selfserve' chooser. Prefill params ?company=, ?name=, ?email= pass through in ANY environment and are display-only.

The five client personas (lib/onboarding-entry.ts:23-28, :79-85): selfserve, retainer, project, existing_project, existing_retainer, each fixing engagement (project|retainer), clientType (new|existing), entry (selfserve|invited) and hasEngagement.

Step assembly (components/tahi/onboarding-content.tsx:94-103): existing+project -> ['welcome','kickoff']; existing+retainer -> ['welcome','plan','pay']; new+project -> ['welcome','details','invite','kickoff']; new+retainer -> ['welcome','plan','pay','details','invite']. Step labels come from META (:76-79): welcome 'Welcome', plan 'Your plan', pay 'Payment', details 'Confirm you', work 'Your brief', invite 'Your team', kickoff 'Kickoff', orient 'Welcome'.

Self-serve chooser (onboarding-content.tsx:433-478, only when clientType 'new' AND entry 'selfserve' AND not yet chosen): two cards, 'Ongoing design & build' (jumps straight into the retainer steps) and 'A one-off project' (an enquiry form). The enquiry form fields are Company name (required), Website, brief textarea (required), Rough budget select (BUDGETS, :71) and discipline select (DISCIPLINES, :72); it POSTs /api/portal/enquiry and shows a success screen 'Thanks, we\'re on it.' (:435-441).

Onboarding plan step (onboarding-content.tsx:516-545) hardcodes two plans in the file — Maintain $1,500 base / $1,000 track and Scale $4,000 base / $1,500 track (PLANS, :67-70) — plus a parallel-track add-on checkbox and the ANCHOR copy 'Hiring the equivalent specialists separately runs $5,200 to $17,500+ a month.' (:71). These are NOT read from the admin plan catalogue that /api/portal/subscription serves to the settings Plan section.

Onboarding pay step delegates to <OnboardingPayment> (Stripe PaymentElement) which renders its own footer (onboarding-content.tsx:546-562). 'Invoice me' routes through POST /api/onboarding/complete with billingMode 'invoice', which records organisations.paymentTerms, raises a DRAFT invoice priced server-side from STRIPE_PLANS, notifies all admins and writes an audit row (app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts:108-241).

POST /api/onboarding/complete is an ENTITLEMENT gate, not a flag setter (route.ts:36-51). It only writes publicMetadata.onboardingComplete when the caller is a teammate, consumed an invite (:280-291), is on recorded net terms (:296-307), holds an active/trialing/past_due subscription (:311-323), or Stripe confirms one live despite webhook lag (:328-345). Otherwise 402 `{ok:false, reason:'not-entitled'}` (:348-351). With no org it returns `{ok:false, reason:'no-org'}` 200 (:250).

The dashboard layout re-checks the same flag: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:62-71 reads Clerk publicMetadata.onboardingComplete for non-admins and redirects to /onboarding at :88, failing OPEN on a Clerk error. Contact backfill (linkContactOnSignIn) runs BEFORE that redirect on purpose (:86, with the reasoning at :73-85).

Middleware onboarding handling: middleware.ts:150-177 stashes ?token= into an httpOnly 1-hour `tahi-invite-token` cookie on /onboarding and /welcome and redirects unauthenticated visitors to /sign-in with redirect_url. middleware.ts:205-209 confines any signed-in user with NO org to the onboarding flow.

reads.summary:
Complete map of the client (portal) audience across Overview home, /requests list, /requests/[id] detail and the New request dialog, plus the portal APIs behind them, the feature gates and the mobile shell.

Shape of the surface today. A client session is anything whose Clerk org is not NEXT_PUBLIC_TAHI_ORG_ID. The dashboard layout resolves permissions server-side, force-redirects an unfinished client to /onboarding, and renders a 5-item client nav (Overview, Requests, Files, Services, Invoices-if-org-admin) plus a 3-tab + More mobile bar. /overview switches to ClientHome; /requests renders the SAME shared RequestList/RequestDetail components the studio uses, with the client branches selected by `isAdmin === false` rather than a separate portal component tree. That sharing is the single biggest source of the problems below: the portal API returns a deliberately narrow client-safe projection, but the shared components were written against the admin projection, so a dozen fields the client UI reads are simply `undefined` and the UI silently renders the "nothing here" branch.

Four structural findings a redesign has to decide about:
1. Two different status vocabularies. The client HOME translates statuses into client words (Queued / In build / Review / Delivered), the client LIST and DETAIL show the raw studio labels (Submitted / In Review / Client Review / On Hold). Same request, two names, one click apart.
2. The detail page lies about people and structure. /api/portal/requests/[id] returns no `participants`, no `subRequests`, no `parent`, no `orgName`, no `assigneeName`, no `unreadCount` and no `formResponses` — but the detail renders a People card ("No PM assigned / No assignees yet / No followers yet"), hides the sub-request panel, and drops the breadcrumb parent. Meanwhile the LIST route DOES return participants and sub-request counts, so a client sees avatars and an expand chevron on the list and an empty People card on the item they just opened.
3. Loading states are missing on the home (TASKS.md CT.3b is open). Every client-home card except Invoices renders its empty-state copy while its fetch is in flight, so a real client sees "No requests yet", "Nothing waiting on you", "0 open" for the first round trip.
4. Every "new request" affordance on the home routes to `/requests` (the list), not to the dialog — the dialog only opens on `?new=1`. So the client home's primary CTA is a two-click menu that lands on a list.

Client write surface is exactly four things: submit a request (POST /api/portal/requests), post a message on a request, approve / request-changes a delivery in client_review, upload a file to a request, plus reordering a track queue and ticking first-run steps from the home. Everything else is read-only by construction.

## What a client can reach today

**Invoices** is one shared component tree branched on `isAdmin`, not a separate portal surface. `/invoices` renders `InvoiceList` (1381 lines, mostly the admin create slide-over); `/invoices/[id]` renders `InvoiceDetail` (1153 lines, mostly admin actions). The client audience gets: a filter bar + DataTable (amount, status, due, created, Pay now) with a bespoke mobile card below `md`; and a detail page with a hero amount, a status pill, a metadata grid, an optional Stripe "Pay <amount>" CTA, notes, line items and totals. Three honest denial states (member seat / feature disabled / unlinked login) are already wired through `lib/portal-admin-label.ts`, and they are the best-written thing on the surface.

**Pay now is Stripe-only.** `payUrl` on both portal routes is `invoices.stripeHostedInvoiceUrl` and nothing else. `invoices.xeroOnlineInvoiceUrl` exists in the schema (migration 0091), is captured by the Xero syncs, and is selected by **zero** client-facing code. `lib/invoice-pay-settings.ts` defines and validates `invoicing.bankDetails`, `invoicing.xeroPaymentAccountCode` and `invoicing.xeroEmailMode`, and its own header says the "How to pay" block is "next slice". The string "How to pay" appears only in comments. So IC.4a landed the **server half**: column, validators, capture, settings PATCH. The client half (a How to pay block, a Xero pay link, a settings form to type the bank details into) does not exist. **A Xero-rail client today sees an amount, a due date, and no way to pay.**

**Services** is a two-branch page with a nine-field read-only card grid. There is no org scoping (`showInCatalog = 1` studio-wide, `select()` with no projection), no "who it is for", no "what you get", no "from" price semantics, no CTA of any kind, and no admin nav entry to edit it from. The `services` table carries name, description, price (cents), currency, isRecurring, recurringInterval, showInCatalog, category. That is the whole content model.

**The upsell machinery for CL.3 already exists elsewhere and is worth reusing rather than inventing.** `components/tahi/settings/sections/plan.tsx` (Settings > Plan & billing, client audience) is a working plan-aware upsell: it reads `GET /api/portal/subscription` (which returns `clientType: 'retainer' | 'project'` plus the admin-edited `plan_catalog`), renders a plan grid with tag/features/price/"Most popular", and every CTA posts `POST /api/portal/subscription/change-request`, which mutates nothing, notifies the whole studio and writes an audit entry. It ends with the exact CL.3 escape hatch: "Need something bigger, or a custom scope? Send us a request." → `/requests?new=1`. That is the "Ask about this" pattern, already built, already honest, sitting on a page nobody navigates to from the client rail.

decisions: Client status vocabulary is three words, not seven. Awaiting payment, Overdue, Paid. Draft and Written off are studio accounting words and never render; overdue stays derived from the due date and is never a stored status, so a viewed-but-late invoice cannot badge itself wrong.

PROPOSED, needs schema: invoices.number. One real invoice number (INV-2026-014) used in the breadcrumb, the page title, the metadata, the email and the bank reference. Today the surface slices the id at 6 chars in the breadcrumb, 8 in the metadata and 8 in the email, so a client reading the reference off the page quotes something that matches nothing. IC.7 already owes this and the How to pay block cannot ship honestly without it.

PROPOSED, wire the existing column: payUrl resolves stripeHostedInvoiceUrl OR xeroOnlineInvoiceUrl. The Xero link is captured by the syncs today and read by zero client code. Treat NULL as normal (Xero only issues it once the invoice is AUTHORISED) and never cache it: the design falls through to How to pay rather than showing a dead action area.

How to pay is the fallback, never the second-class option. Amount, due date, bank name, account name, account number and the invoice number as the reference, each with its own Copy, plus Copy all details, plus a soft "Pay by card instead" that opens the ask sheet. It reads from the invoicing.bankDetails setting that lib/invoice-pay-settings.ts already validates. A Xero-rail client is never left with an amount and no way to act.

Amounts are never converted. Every figure renders in the invoice's own currency with an explicit symbol (NZ$, US$), and the top bar display-currency context is deliberately not consulted, because the portal has no exchange rates and today's code silently relabels an unconverted NZD figure as US$. A USD client just works: money(amount, currency) reads the invoice.

No figure survives a state where the data did not. During loading and after a failed load the tiles, the counts, the filter chips and the overdue callout all stand down, and the error copy says so out loud. The live surface currently shows real totals above a "could not load" panel.

A question is a first class action on the invoice, not a reply-to-this-email footnote. Every line item carries an always-visible Ask, and the whole invoice carries a thread. PROPOSED: this creates a request-thread conversation scoped to the invoice (or, until conversations land, a category-admin request titled "Question about INV-..." carrying the invoiceId), and the copy promises the invoice waits while it is answered.

One AskSheet serves both surfaces, and it is explicit about consequence. "Start a request" says it joins your queue; "Just a question" says nothing enters your queue. The invoice asks are question-only; a service ask offers both. This reuses the honesty of the existing /api/portal/subscription/change-request pattern (notify the studio, mutate nothing) rather than inventing a second promise.

Read only is belt and braces, matching client-home.tsx. Under impersonation every Pay now, every Ask and every plan control is a disabled button with a stated reason, so an admin previewing a client can never reach a live hosted payment page from Invoices. The live list and detail have no such guard today.

Services carries no prices at all, and says why: "No prices here on purpose. Every one of these is scoped and quoted for Mahana Orchards before a single hour is booked." The only money on the page is the client's own bill (their plan rate and the add ons on their account), which is a fact of their invoice rather than a pitch. Liam still owes the upsell brief; nothing here pre-empts it.

PROPOSED, needs schema: the services table has name, description, price, currency, recurring, category and a catalogue flag, and nothing else. This design needs outcome, includes[], timeline, fit ('plan' | 'addon' | 'project') and a per-client forYou note, plus org scoping (CT.11) before it can ship: today every client sees every catalogue row.

Fit is the card's honest hook instead of a price. In your plan (submit it as a request, it joins your queue) / Add on (a monthly line beside the retainer) / Project (scoped and quoted on its own). Each card carries exactly one soft CTA, and the hint under it repeats the consequence.

Your plan sits above the catalogue, not in Settings. The working plan upsell in components/tahi/settings/sections/plan.tsx is reachable only from the sidebar user card. This design brings the plan, the tracks, the next invoice and the add ons onto a page the client can actually navigate to, and keeps the change path as a conversation rather than a self-serve switch.
Nothing to create anywhere. No admin editor, no "add a service", no price fields. The studio-side catalogue editor is a separate surface and is out of scope by instruction.

Narrow first with container queries, not viewport media queries, because the shell frames mobile at 390px inside a desktop viewport. .pm is the query container, the base rules ARE the 375px layout, and 46rem upgrades to the table. Verified at 375 with zero horizontal overflow, and at 1280 in light and dark.

Both dividers and borders follow the house rule. Cards are bordered on all sides; row separators use the shell's own sibling pattern (.pm-row + .pm-row) so nothing is a one-sided box border. Leaf radius is reserved for primary CTAs, icon tiles and avatar wrappers.

Tone colours are declared once at .pm scope with a dark override, so no component hardcodes a hex and dark mode falls out of the tokens. One extra dark rule: a filled brand button gets dark ink in dark mode, because --brand lightens and white on it fails contrast.
openQuestions: The signed-in client here is Mahana Orchards / Jordan Reeve. The shell's PROFILES.client is Jordan Reeve at Acme and requests-audience.jsx pins CLIENT_ORG to Physitrack, so the prototype currently carries three client identities. Which one wins? Download PDF and Download receipt are drawn on both the list and the detail, and neither exists in the product. Do you want a PDF pipeline in scope for this slice, or should those two buttons come out until there is a file to hand over?

A question about an invoice: should it create a real request in the client's queue (visible in Requests, counts against nothing), or a studio-only thread that never appears in their request list? The design currently promises the second, and says so in the copy.

Three things the design leans on that the product does not have yet, in the order they block: invoices.number (nothing else can be an honest bank reference), xeroOnlineInvoiceUrl read on the client side, and a richer, org-scoped services content model. There is no size limit and no MIME allowlist in the product, and the proxy buffers the whole body in worker memory so a large file dies with an opaque 500 behind a generic toast. The sample batch deliberately includes a 700 MB .mov that fails with Larger than the 500 MB limit and offers Remove, not a futile Retry. A connection failure is the opposite: it offers Retry and the retry gets through.

Uploads run in parallel with per-file percent, not the current serial loop behind a button that only says Uploading. The tray is a bottom-right panel with a meter per row, cancel while running, and an N of M added header.

Drag and drop is real, and the drop veil names its destination. The request-detail Files panel already promises Drop one here with no drop handler behind it; this is the promise kept, and dropping into a folder puts the file in that folder.
Storage meter is a proposal (there is no quota today), used to replace the invisible 100-row ceiling with something honest. It sits at the foot of the folder tree.

Messages keeps the org channel as the client's one standing line to the studio, pinned above the per-request threads. The studio line is auto-marked read on open, mirroring the portal conversations GET that writes lastReadAt, and the NEW divider survives that so the client still sees where they left off.

The unread cursor is drawn twice on purpose: a count pill on the conversation row, and a NEW rule inside the thread at the first message the client had not seen. That is conversationParticipants.lastReadAt used properly.

Voice notes are surfaced for clients for the first time. The voiceNotes table exists and works but is only reachable behind the hidden Messages page, and the live request thread has no microphone. Player has play/pause, a waveform scrub, a countdown and a 1x/1.5x/2x speed control.

The studio composer has Reply to the client and Internal note as two visible tabs, not a hidden switch, and the internal bubble is amber so an internal note can never be mistaken for something the client saw.

Request threads in Messages and the thread on the request detail are one conversation, not two. Every request_thread row carries an Open the request button. That only holds if the portal messages POST starts persisting conversationId, which it does not today: client replies get conversationId null and would silently vanish from the conversation view.

designs.notes:
All four files were already in the project from an earlier pass of this brief; this run verified them in a browser and fixed four real defects. The scratch harness is portal-files-preview.html, left in place: it mounts both pages standalone against the DS bundle plus app-shell.css and has toggles for page, audience, state, theme, width and View as client.

Verified live at 1280 and at 375 (inside a scaled iframe, since the machine's screen caps the window at 757 CSS px), in light and dark, on both audiences and in the read-only lens. No console errors.

Defects found and fixed:
1. FileCard, FileRow and the conversation row were declared inside their page bodies, so every parent render produced a new component type and tore down the subtree. Any open kebab menu died the moment a toast expired or a letter landed in the search box. Proven before the fix (menu open, one keystroke that did not filter the card out, menu gone) and proven fixed after. All three are now hoisted to module scope and take props.
2. The Messages thread did not scroll to its newest message on first paint. The scroll effect ran while the pane was still a skeleton and the ref was null, and its deps never changed again, so scrollTop stayed 0 and the last message sat under the composer. Measured: scrollTop 0 of a 599px scrollHeight in a 550px box. Fixed by adding state to the deps; now lands at the bottom.
3. Upload Retry reset the row to 0 percent and never restarted the progress loop, so a retried upload hung forever. Rewritten around a reusable tick, plus a retried flag so a connection failure succeeds on the second go while an over-the-cap file keeps failing and now offers Remove rather than a pointless Retry. Verified end to end: 2 done, 1 hard failure, library count 22 to 24, retry resumes.
4. The empty demo state left the folder tree showing 22 files and the storage meter showing 333 MB beside a Nothing here yet page. The tree, the mobile folder strip and the meter now read from the same source and all go to zero.

Smaller polish in the same pass: the finished-upload row is now appended by an effect rather than by a setState inside another setState's updater; the client switcher uses a down chevron instead of a right caret; the comment toast is audience-aware rather than always saying the studio has been told; the Cmd plus Enter hint is hidden under md and on coarse pointers with the Send button taking over the right-hand push; and the voice waveform is drawn from the text ramp instead of --border, which was nearly invisible on the dark surface.

Mobile audit at 375: no interactive element measures under 44px anywhere on either page (checked every button, icon button, lens chip and folder chip programmatically), no horizontal scroll, the drawer becomes a bottom sheet with a grab handle and safe-area padding on its footer, and the folder tree collapses to a scrollable chip strip.

House rules held throughout: rem spacing only, shell theme tokens rather than hardcoded hex (the two exceptions are the shared danger red and the amber internal tone, both used as literals the way the rest of the prototype does), leaf radius reserved for primary CTAs, folder and empty-state icon wells and the studio channel mark, hairlines drawn as full-width pseudo-elements rather than single-side borders, hover plus focus on every control, nothing revealed by hover alone, and no em or en dashes.

One environment caveat worth knowing if the integrator re-tests: Chrome throttles background tabs to roughly one timer tick per second, so the simulated uploads crawl when the preview tab is not frontmost. The behaviour is correct, just slow.

Two things this design assumes the product does not have and would need before the surface is true rather than merely drawn: a folder column plus a folders table, and a file-scoped conversation. Both are called out in decisions. The known leak on the portal request-files route (attachments on internal or soft-deleted studio notes are listed to the client) is not something a redesign can close; it stays a backend fix.

decisions: NEW SURFACE. There is no /notifications route in the product at all: the whole surface today is the bell popover. This page is a proposal, and it needs a back end change before it can ship. GET /api/notifications is a hard PAGE_SIZE 20 with no page, cursor, limit, read-state, kind or date parameter, so neither the Past tab nor Load older can be built on it as written. The design assumes the route grows ?cursor= &limit= &read= &kind= &range=.

All vs Past is proposed as the last thirty days versus everything older, grouped by day in All and by month in Past. Nothing in the API expresses a date range today, so this is a proposal, and the copy commits to it out loud ('That is the last thirty days. Anything older sits under Past.' / 'We keep twelve months.').

Filters are by KIND, not by the 30 NotificationEventType values, which are an internal vocabulary no client should meet. Kinds map onto entityType groups and are audience-scoped: a client gets Requests, Replies, Invoices, Studio notes, Documents; the studio gets Requests, Tasks, Replies, Invoices, Calls, Sales, System. Each kind wears the shell's own nav glyph, so a request notification wears the Requests icon the rail wears.

HONEST DEEP LINKS, the main design decision here. lib/notification-links.ts returns null for a client on documents, tasks, calls, deals, schedules and contracts. Rather than render a link that bounces them, those rows are drawn as a statement with 'Nothing to open yet' and no button wrapper, so the row is not clickable at all. The sample data carries one (the signed NDA) so the state is visible.

Opening a row marks it read optimistically and then navigates. Today only the request detail page clears the bell (request-detail.tsx:840-863), so an invoice or announcement stays unread forever. Doing it on the row itself closes that hole without touching every destination page.

Mark as read is offered per row and for all; unread, delete and archive are NOT offered, because `read` is a one-way flag in the API and there is no endpoint for any of them. Better to ship three honest verbs than four with one that lies.
The counts are suppressed while the page is loading or errored, and the whole kind-filter row is withheld until real rows land. A page that says 'Requests 5' before the read returns is guessing.

ACCOUNT is proposed as one scrolling page (You, Sign-in, What reaches you, Your team, Sign out) rather than the studio's settings rail. A client has four things to change, not fourteen, and the rail costs a click per section on a phone. Sticky anchor chips give the same jump without the sidebar. Wire it so the client `settings` route lands here, so the user card and the mobile More sheet keep working unchanged.

SIGN-IN AND SECURITY IS ENTIRELY NEW. No Clerk UserProfile or UserButton is mounted anywhere in the product; a client cannot change their email, password or 2FA from any screen, and the profile page's disabled email field points vaguely at 'your login provider' with no link. Designed as three rows that open a panel and hand off, plus a two-step row that is honestly labelled Off. If the hand-off is to Clerk's own hosted screens, the panels become links and the copy still holds.

PORTAL ROLES IN PLAIN WORDS. Owner / Admin / Member, each with a one-line gloss on the pill and a legend under the roster: 'Can invite people, change the plan, and see invoices' beats the word Admin. Owner is the primary contact rather than a portalRole value, so its row menu offers no level change and says 'The main contact cannot be changed here. Ask the studio and we will move it for you.', which matches the API's 409. The design deliberately does not offer a Viewer level: it has no portalRole backing.

PREFERENCES LIST ONLY WHAT ACTUALLY SENDS. Four rows: Request updates, Replies, Invoices, Studio notes. 'Delivery ready' and 'Weekly summary' are dropped because they are quarantined event types no send path resolves, so both switches in the live UI are inert. 'Studio notes' (announcement_posted) is ADDED because it is a real preference the announcement email path reads and there is no way to mute it today. Mentions are not a separate row because notifyMentionedPerson writes type 'new_message', so muting replies already mutes mentions.

Quiet hours is kept but reworded to a promise a reader could keep ('Nothing lands in your inbox between 7pm and 8am. Invoices and anything waiting on you still come through.'). It is write-only in the product right now with zero readers, so it must either land with a reader or not ship. Flagged rather than quietly reproduced.

WELCOME IS THE ROOM, NOT THE NUDGE. portal-home already renders a compact first-run panel on the overview, so this page does not duplicate it: it is the destination behind that panel, carrying the two things a four-line checklist cannot, the studio intro cards for Liam and Staci and the actual video. Four steps matching Tahi Onboarding.html: sign-in already done, meet the team, watch the welcome, make your first request.

The welcome video is drawn as a real player tile with a play control, a duration and a captions note. The live onboarding 'video' is a still image with a setInterval caption ticker over a hardcoded script and no media element. If there is no Loom to embed yet, the tile is the placeholder, but it must not pretend to play.

OFFLINE gains a retry button, a 'still nothing' follow-up, a back-online state and a two-line reassurance that submitted work is safe. The live page is a terminal screen whose only exit is a browser reload. Two product notes for whoever builds it: /offline is not in middleware's public route list, so a signed-out navigation redirects to /sign-in, which means the service worker's Cache.addAll of '/offline' can reject at install and leave exactly the users who need it with no fallback at all.

375 ROW ANATOMY. critique.summary:
Reviewed all thirteen client surfaces at 1280 and 375, light and dark, driven live in Chromium. Zero console or page errors on any run, which matches the integrator's report: the wiring is sound. The design is not, yet, and almost all of the damage traces to two problems that sit underneath the individual pages.

First, a CSS namespace collision. portal-home.css and portal-files.css both claim the `pf-` prefix and redefine 47 of the same class names, including .pf-grid, .pf-card, .pf-row, .pf-av, .pf-btn and .pf-tabs; portal-files.css loads second and wins. Separately portal-files.css `.pm-row` (the Messages conversation row) is overwritten by portal-money.css `.pm-row` (the invoice row). Measured consequences: the Your work in motion card is 1074px inside a 1040px scroller and loses 52px off the right edge; Recently delivered, Recent files, Your team, The pieces of this request and Files on this request all render with a 470px empty column and titles clamped to 128px; the Files grid view collapses to one giant card per row; the Messages conversation list is laid out by the invoice table at both widths and is unusable at 375; every avatar wrapper on Home, Requests and Onboarding loses the leaf radius and becomes a circle; and the phone tab bar picks up a border, a 10px radius and a 14px bottom margin that pushes it 2px off the bottom of the screen. Fixing the prefixes fixes most of this list at once, so it should be done before any per-page polish.

Second, there is no shared data spine. Four different signed-in identities appear across one portal: Jordan Reeve at Acme in the rail card, Ana Rewiri at Mahana Orchards on Home and Account, Jordan Reeve at Physitrack in Files and Messages, and Mahana Orchards on a different plan in Services. Home says Scale, NZ$4,800 a month, two tracks; Services says Maintain, NZ$1,500, one track. Home's 'Pay now' points at INV-2087 for NZ$4,800, which does not exist on the Invoices page. TR-1042 and TR-1028 have different titles depending on which page you are on, so every request thread in Messages is a broken link. One client fixture imported by all four modules resolves it.

Three things need attention beyond that. Schedule, Contracts and Proposals are still in the client nav and fall through to the studio's PageBody, which shows a client three other clients by name (Acme, Northwind, Kowtow) with statuses; that route must be closed to the client audience. On the request detail at 375 the sticky Approve and Changes buttons render at y714-758 under a tab bar occupying y740-814, so the portal's two most important actions are partly covered by the nav. And New request is silently dead from the request detail at both widths, including the phone '+' tab, verified with no errors thrown.

The States debug pill in portal-money is still live and overlaps the rail user card at 1280 and a real CTA at 375; delete targets are listed on the invoices entry.

What is genuinely good: the writing is the best I have seen in this project, particularly on request detail, invoice detail and the account level legend. Invoice detail is ship-ready. Account is one identity fix and one overflow fix away. Home's composition, the dark hero tile and the plain-language status rail are the right direction. Dark mode holds up across every page, with card contrast measured at 14.3:1 and no regressions found; the one weakness is that the Home hero tile flattens into the page background. No em or en dashes in any portal copy, and no internal chrome leaks into the client's Messages view. The remaining consistency work is small and specific: three of the four modules use a near-black active filter chip while Account uses brand green, primary CTAs carry the leaf radius on Home and Requests but not on the new-request dialog, Pay now, or Meet the team, and portal-files.css ships one focus-visible rule against 23, 18 and 12 in the other three.
